issues.issue: The parenthetical '(including, but not limited to, recoveries in respect of the representations and warranties made by the Seller pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement)' is attached to 'estimated expenses', so whether repurchase recoveries are Subsequent Recoveries turns on a misplaced clause.
The term is said to have the meaning ascribed 'pursuant to Section 2.03(d)', but Section 2.03 has only subsections (a) and (b) and defines the Substitution Adjustment Amount in unlettered text.

This definition states that the Supplemental Interest Trust, Swap Agreement, Swap Account and Swap Administration Agreement 'do not constitute parts of the Trust Fund', while the 'Trust or Trust Fund' definition includes at clause (vi) 'the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates'.

Limb (i) sets the trigger at a percentage 'of the Current Specified Enhancement Percentage' rather than of a balance, and the measuring date is garbled ('as of the as of the last day of the related Due Period'), leaving the test hard to apply.

Clause (vi) puts 'the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates' into the Trust Fund, while the Supplemental Interest Trust definition says the Swap Administration Agreement does 'not constitute parts of the Trust Fund'.
The stated allocation is 93% plus 3% plus 1% to each of five named Classes, which totals 101% of the Voting Rights and cannot be applied as written.

This agreement is said to be 'attached hereto as Exhibit R-3', the same exhibit the Saxon Assignment Agreement definition claims, while the exhibit list assigns R-2 to Saxon; two definitions point at one exhibit.
The definition reads 'the cap contract, dated Agreement Provider', omitting both the date and the counterparty, so the instrument is identified only by the exhibit reference.
The conveyance is of 'the assets in the Mortgage Loans', an odd formulation that leaves unclear whether the Sellers conveyed the loans themselves or some lesser interest in them.

The proviso says 'the Seller may deliver the following documents', but each lettered alternative that follows says 'the Depositor may deliver', so who bears the delivery obligation for substitute documents is inconsistent within the same sentence.

The closing sentence makes cure, repurchase or substitution 'the sole remedies respecting such defect', but limits itself to 'a defect in a constituent document', leaving open whether it also bars remedies for breach of representation.
The sole-remedy sentence sits against Section 2.02(d), which directs the Trustee to enforce 'any other obligations' of the Sellers and Originators under the purchase and Bring Down Agreements.

The Trustee's enforcement duty extends beyond repurchase, cure and substitution to 'any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation' the Sponsor's Accredited backstop, a catch-all of uncertain reach.
This enforcement duty must be reconciled with Section 2.02(c), which declares cure, repurchase or substitution to be the 'sole remedies' available on behalf of Certificateholders.
